paragraphs.source_en: Dawn came early in summer, and before long the eastern sky was beginning to brighten. The lady thought that the rain had stopped and it looked as though the day would be fine again. In the waterway that wound from the Horikawa by Sanjō Castle all the way to Honnō-ji, water lilies dotted the surface of the clear blue-green water. How beautiful they would be when touched by the violet glow of dawn in the sky! All at once, she felt certain that they would prevail.

paragraphs.source_en: When Lady Nō first married Nobunaga, she had intended to kill him in his sleep; yet at some point, without knowing when, she had become an ordinary wife attentive to her husband, and then had come to know a wife's despair. Nobunaga could never belong to a wife. He was a man whose appetite only grew with every conquest and who could never be satisfied. She had always feared that the tenuous thread of affection binding them would snap. But Mitsuhide's unexpected rebellion had changed all of that.
